We have supported the development of the North East Carbon and Nature Marketplace (NECaNM), which officially launched in May 2025. This North East focused marketplace will provide opportunities for the Council to act as both a seller and buyer of carbon and other environmental credits within the North East region.
The NECaNM is designed to:
· Power the North East's Net Zero Transition by enabling investment in measurable, local carbon reduction projects.
· Raise the Integrity Standard by ensuring transparency, accountability, and additionality in all listed projects.
· Maximise Regional Benefits by reinvesting carbon finance into local communities, creating green jobs, and restoring landscapes.
It will deliver co-benefits beyond carbon reduction including improved air and water quality, enhanced physical and mental health, the creation of skilled green jobs, and increased biodiversity. It will also empower local communities by supporting projects that are visible, tangible, and rooted in place—helping residents see and feel the benefits of climate action.

1. First Phase (2015-2017)

 - 25 basic environmental facilities received annual allocation of 1.21 million tons (91.12% of 2014-2016 average emissions).

3. Third Phase (2021-2025)
 - Allocation for 2021-2022: 80.28% of past emissions (over 10% reduction from previous phase).
 - Despite tighter allocations, Daegu achieved surplus trading results:
 - 2022: Net sale of 12,521 tons → Revenue ~170 million KRW; Carry-over: 25,141 tons
 - 2023: Net sale of 11,248 tons → Revenue ~100 million KRW; Carry-over: 23,098 tons
 - 2024: Net sale of 1,62 tons → Revenue ~10 million KRW; Carry-over: 5,104 tons

column19: In 2019, Portugal published its 2050 Roadmap to Carbon Neutrality (RNC20250), which sets out the long-term strategy for a sustainable, zero-carbon economy by 2050. The RNC250 brings together a range of energy and mobility policies that can reduce greenhouse gas emissions by around 85 per cent compared to 2015 and increase carbon sequestration by expanding and strengthening the ecosystem services provided by land use and forestry to offset the remaining 15 per cent of emissions. Within this remit, the FUN Porto (Native Urban Forests) project aims to produce native trees and shrubs for strategic planting in the city, citizen participation in private spaces and export for ecological restoration in surrounding regions. The initiative aims to offset a significant amount of CO2 (at least 9,877 tonnes/year) through strategic tree planting, contributing to urban greening and ecological restoration. However, it should also be noted that Porto is a city with a very limited territory (42 km2) and very densely urbanised (historic city and World Heritage Site), which limits carbon offsetting within its territorial limits, despite efforts to promote nature-based solutions in all their aspects and on all possible surfaces. Therefore, the main solution that the city intends to use to offset most of its residual emissions is the Voluntary Carbon Market (in Portugal), recently established by Law No. 4/2024 of 5 January, which opens the possibility of establishing carbon offset projects in the national territory. These projects aim to use nature-based solutions for carbon sequestration, while providing important benefits for the protection of biodiversity and natural capital, for the regulation of various natural cycles, for landscape design and for interventions in territories, especially the most vulnerable, and also contributing to adaptation to climate change by increasing the resilience of the national territory. This law, which is still subject to specific regulations, is of great interest to cities such as Porto, which want to offset their carbon emissions and at the same time hope to have the most positive impact on the surrounding territory (the North region of Porto). The city will therefore take advantage of this new regulation and develop a comprehensive strategy based on it in the coming years.

Both strengthening local carbon sinks and developing offsetting measures are emphasized in the Turku Climate Plan. Turku has an active role in several research and development projects in these fields. 

Turku participated in the KUNTANIELU research project, alongside three other cities, the Finnish Environment Institute (Syke), Natural Resources Institute Finland (Luke), and the University of Helsinki. The project, under the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry's Catch the Carbon program, aimed to help municipalities increase net carbon sinks in the land use sector and establish municipal-level offsetting. It provided guidance on verifying carbon sinks, enhanced knowledge for implementing offsetting, and explored the potential for linking municipal carbon offsetting to voluntary ecological compensation. More information provided here: https://www.turku.fi/sites/default/files/document/land-use-strategies-for-climate-action-and-biodiversity_kuntanielu.pdf.

A compra e venda de créditos de carbono de forma mais massificada por parte da autarquia não foi considerada para alcance do “net zero target” em 2030 (Roteiro/PMAC 2030), mas esta opção é uma oportunidade para mais rápido alcançar a neutralidade carbónica.
Importa referir que o enquadramento legal para a implementação de um mercado voluntário de carbono a nível nacional foi apenas criado este ano, 2024, com a publicação do Decreto-Lei n.º 4/2024, de 5 de janeiro.
Através deste novo regime, os Municípios e outras entidades terão oportunidade de adquirir créditos de carbono, como forma de compensar as emissões de gases poluentes que não conseguem reduzir ou evitar, mas também de valorizar os seus investimentos em projetos ou soluções desenvolvidas para redução ou eliminação da pegada carbónica.
Não obstante Matosinhos tem um piloto da plataforma AYR, uma plataforma de aceleração da sustentabilidade para ajudar a atingir objetivos de carbono zero.
Concebido para ligar comunidades, pessoas e coisas numa rede onde as ações sustentáveis criam tokens criptográficos que podem ser trocados por bens e serviços verdes ou utilizados para compensar localmente as emissões de carbono.
Este projeto funciona pela seleção de um transporte 'verde' que evita as emissões de CO2. O crédito 
AYR é recebido em função das emissões de CO2 evitadas, sendo que posteriormente o crypto token de crédito AYR pode ser utilizado para outros passeios e mercadorias.

column18:
Berdasarkan rencana Afvalzorg dan Multriwell, skema proyek TPA Terjun direncanakan berjalan dalam beberapa tahap yaitu:
1. Tahap 1 - Persetujuan Prinsip : Persetujuan dari KLHK terkait penjualan kredit karbon internasional dengan estimasi waktu ± 3 bulan.
2. Tahap 2 - Studi Kelayakan (Feasibility Study) :	Perhitungan teknis, finansial, dan verifikasi awal dengan estimasi waktu ± 3 bulan.
3. Tahap 3 - Registrasi & Verifikasi Awal : Registrasi proyek di standar internasional seperti VCS (Verified Carbon Standard/Verra) dengan estimasi waktu ± 6 bulan.
4. Tahap 4 - Periode Kredit Aktif: Kredit mulai diterbitkan dari pengurangan emisi gas TPA yang terukur dengan estimasi waktu minimal 7-10 tahun (standar VCS untuk proyek LFG biasanya 7 tahun dan dapat diperpanjang).

Negara/Wilayah calon pembeli internasional yaitu :
1. Calon pembeli pertama adalah Korea Selatan.
Korea Selatan memiliki kewajiban pengurangan emisi melalui K-ETS (Korea Emissions Trading Scheme), sehingga mereka membutuhkan kredit karbon dari luar negeri.
2. Calon pembeli kedua adalah Swiss (Eropa).
Swiss secara aktif membeli kredit karbon dari negara berkembang untuk memenuhi komitmen Perjanjian Paris (Paris Agreement).
3. Calon pembeli ketiga adalah Belanda (Uni Eropa).
Pemerintah Belanda mendukung proyek persampahan berkelanjutan sebagai bagian dari program Net Zero Emission Uni Eropa.

Saat ini Pemerintah Kota Medan berencana melakukan Penjualan Kredit Karbon TPA Berkelanjutan, jumlah emisi yang berpotensi dijual sebagai kredit karbon berasal dari gas TPA (landfill gas) di TPA Terjun.

Rincian Emisi
- Kapasitas produksi gas TPA Terjun: 4.500 m³/jam
- Jika dikonversi ke karbon dioksida (CO₂): ≈392.000 ton CO₂ per tahun (Setara dengan emisi dari ±85.000 mobil per tahun).

1. Angka 392.000 ton CO₂ per tahun merupakan potensi total emisi yang dapat diolah dan dijual sebagai kredit karbon setelah dilakukan penangkapan dan pembakaran (flaring) gas metana di TPA.
2. Untuk menjual kredit karbon ini, Pemerintah Kota Medan bersama Afvalzorg & Multriwell masih memerlukan:
a. Persetujuan prinsip dari Kementerian Lingkungan Hidup terkait penjualan kredit karbon internasional.
b. Mendapatkan pembeli potensial, yang saat ini sudah mencakup tiga calon pembeli:
- Mitra dari Korea Selatan
- Mitra dari Swiss
- Pemerintah Belanda

SSunderland already benefits from some natural offsetting. In 2023, the Forestry sector sequestered 7,000tCO2. Sunderland City Council are currently working to implement the Green Infrastructure Strategy and the Green Infrastructure Action and Delivery Plan, in addition to a number of tree planting projects such as the North East Community Forest. This will also increase natural offsetting.

Aside this, and in line with science-based recommendations provided by the Tyndall Centre and the Council's commitment to the revised UK100 pledge, Sunderland's priority is currently to reduce emissions at source before looking to offset or purchase carbon credits. However, it is widely acknowledged that Sunderland will have some unavoidable emissions and will look to explore the concept of carbon credits in the future.
In March 2024, Sunderland City Council's Cabinet agreed an approach to utilising appropriate Council owned land to deliver biodiversity net gain. Funding to deliver the gain will be secured as part of the planning process which will see the net gain maintained over a minimum 30 year period. Opportunities to build in offsetting / carbon credits in parallel to delivery of Biodiversity Net Gain through this approach will be explored and taken where appropriate.
Sunderland City Council have worked in partnership with the North East Combined Authority (NECA) in establishing the North East Carbon and Nature Marketplace. The Marketplace was launched in June 2025 and provides an online platform where buyers can invest in nature preservation and restoration projects or purchase carbon credits on projects within Sunderland and the wider North East area. Further details are available at https://marketplace.netzeronortheastengland.co.uk/hub

Um componente-chave desta estratégia é o alinhamento com o projeto REDD+ desenvolvido pelo Estado do Tocantins, buscando os seguintes objetivos:

- Estruturar as ações do PMMC e a colaboração com o REDD+ para viabilizar o acesso a recursos via Pagamentos por Serviços Ecossistêmicos (PSE). Planejamos utilizar a remuneração por créditos de carbono, tanto no mercado regulado quanto voluntário, como um dos modelos de financiamento para as atividades propostas.
- Assegurar que as ações de conservação gerem benefícios adicionais, como a proteção da biodiversidade e a promoção do desenvolvimento sustentável para as comunidades locais, conforme previsto na estratégia de infraestrutura verde.

By sourcing carbon credits locally, the municipality ensured that its efforts also supported domestic environmental goals. column19: As an LGU, we recognize that carbon credits may play an important role in our future climate actions, whether through the sale of credits generated from local projects or the purchase of credits to offset emissions we cannot directly reduce. At present, we have completed our GHG inventory, which serves as our starting point. Moving forward, we need to deepen our understanding of national policies and international standards on carbon trading, as well as identify whether our role will be to generate or to purchase credits. From there, we must prepare a clear plan and target—defining the sectors we aim to cover, the possible projects that can yield measurable and verifiable reductions, and the amount of emissions we seek to offset. Establishing a monitoring, reporting, and verification system will be critical to ensure credibility and compliance. We also recognize the need for partnerships with accredited verifiers and project developers, alongside budgetary preparation to support these processes. In the long run, our objective is to align our carbon credit initiatives with national climate commitments, while ensuring that our actions bring co-benefits such as biodiversity protection, community resilience, and livelihood opportunities.

Increase new carbon storage capacity, through the number of trees and hedgerows planted and protected and ensure North Yorkshire has the skilled workforce to manage the increased treescape. There is also potential to develop kelp forests in the marine environment. Preserve existing carbon stores such as peatlands and mature trees, including carbon storage of 'fallen timber'. Support regional partners to develop large scale carbon capture technology and projects around the Humber estuary and at our Energy from Waste plant.\n\nThe council's LINC programme is investigating options to use the market for using natural capital for interventions such as carbon sequestration.

Crediting Area
•	The program covers six provinces under Vietnam's North Central Region Emission Reductions Program, which includes Thừa Thiên Huế among the targeted areas for emissions reduction and carbon sequestration efforts.
•	The total jurisdictional area includes natural forest cover, with projects focused on REDD+ interventions—that is, preventing deforestation and degradation, as well as promoting afforestation and improved forest management.
The offsetting efforts in Thua Thien Hue are taking place within the province's forest lands, as part of a collective effort with a group of provinces in the North Central region of Vietnam.
•	Jurisdictional Area: Thua Thien Hue is one of six provinces in Vietnam's North Central region participating in the World Bank's Forest Carbon Partnership Facility (FCPF) program. This is a jurisdictional-level REDD+ program, meaning the crediting is based on the emission reductions from the entire region, not just individual projects. The other five provinces are Thanh Hoa, Nghe An, Ha Tinh, Quang Binh, and Quang Tri.
•	Specific Locations: Within Thua Thien Hue, the offsetting efforts are focused on the province's natural and planted forests. The activities that contribute to carbon credits include:
o	Reduced Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+): Protecting existing natural forests from being cleared or degraded.
o	Sustainable Forest Management: Implementing practices that enhance the health and carbon stock of forests.
o	Afforestation and Reforestation (ARR): Planting new trees on previously non-forested land to increase carbon sequestration.
column19:
What the North-Central ERP is
•	A jurisdictional REDD+ program under the World Bank's FCPF Carbon Fund, governed by an Emission Reductions Payment Agreement (ERPA) signed Oct 22, 2020. The ERPA envisioned up to 10.3 million tCO₂e in results over a six-year period starting in 2018, for US$51.5 million in results-based payments. 
Where it operates (and Hue's place in it)
•	Country & region: Viet Nam's North Central Region across six provinces — Thanh Hóa, Nghệ An, Hà Tĩnh, Quảng Bình, Quảng Trị, and Thừa Thiên Huế (Hue) — with an ERP accounting area focused on ~2.9 million ha of natural forests. 
•	Hue's ERP area: Hue is explicitly inside the ERP boundary. Provincial implementation is led by each Provincial People's Committee; Hue's eligible forest for ERPA payments was reported at ~204,022 ha (2023). 
What activities/results are credited
•	The ERP credits reductions in deforestation/degradation and enhancement of forest carbon stocks (REDD+) achieved within the six-province landscape. Independent verification under the FCPF framework confirms results before payment. Viet Nam received a US$51.5 million payment for verified ERs on Mar 21, 2024. 
Program timeline & monitoring
•	The ERP's first verified reporting covered 2018-2019 (documented in the program's First ER Monitoring Report). Subsequent reporting covers later years within the ERPA window.
Governance & benefit sharing (how Hue participates)
•	Program entity & coordination: The Viet Nam Forest Protection and Development Fund (VNFF) coordinates nationally and with provinces; provinces (including Hue) oversee on-the-ground implementation and benefit distribution per the Benefit-Sharing Plan (BSP).

•	Country: Viet Nam.

•	Emphasis—Hue's ERP area: Thừa Thiên Huế is explicitly within the ERP jurisdiction; the Government's Sep-2025 Resolution tasks the provincial People's Committees in the North-Central region—including Huế—to coordinate implementation under the ERPA. 
•	Ecosystem scope/hectares: Under the ERPA, the World Bank cites ~2.9 million ha of natural forests across these six provinces as the program's core accounting area for results-based payments. 
Context for this particular transfer
•	The 1.0 Mt transferred in Sep-2025 is drawn from a surplus pool (reported ≈5.91 Mt of ERs from 2018-2019 beyond what was already paid), and is transacted under the 2020 ERPA with IBRD (FCPF Carbon Fund). 
Bottom line: The extra 1,000,000 tCO₂e credits come from verified 2018-2019 REDD+ results within the North-Central ERP—including Thừa Thiên Huế (Hue)—with activities and MRV entirely inside Viet Nam's North Central Region as defined by the program.
column19:
What was approved
•	On 29 Aug 2025, the Government issued Resolution 261/NQ-CP authorizing the transfer of 1.0 million tCO₂e from the North-Central ERP (surplus from 2018-2019) to the World Bank's IBRD under the existing ERPA (signed 22 Oct 2020). The Resolution notes that ≈95% of the transferred credits will be returned to Viet Nam to serve the NDC, and the unit price and other terms follow the ERPA. 
•	The Government News portal's write-up of the resolution reiterates the 1.0 Mt transfer, the 5.91 Mt surplus pool, and the ~95% return clause. 
Where those credits come from (program scope)
•	The North-Central ERP is a jurisdictional REDD+ program covering six provinces, including Thừa Thiên Huế, aimed at reducing deforestation/degradation and enhancing forest carbon stocks. 
•	Coverage includes natural forests (broadleaf evergreen) and plantation forests; press coverage of the 1-million-tonne transfer specifically mentions plantation-forest ERs within the region. 
•	Earlier, Viet Nam received US$51.5m for verified ERs from this same ERP in March 2024, confirming the program's MRV and payments pipeline. 
Hue's ERP area
•	Hue is explicitly part of the ERP jurisdiction. The Government's news note on Resolution 261 tasks provincial authorities in the North-Central region to coordinate implementation and lists “Hue” among those provinces. (Hue's inclusion is clear; some write-ups enumerate five provinces, while World Bank ERP documents specify six provinces for the program overall) 
•	Within the ERP, Hue's forest estate (both natural and plantation areas) is inside the accounting boundary for ERs; key conservation areas tied to cross-border biodiversity corridors include the Sao La (saola) Nature Reserve in Thừa Thiên Huế, which sits within the ERP landscape. 
•	Hue's provincial agencies have been implementing ERP components locally (e.g., benefit-sharing plan consultations/trainings in 2020), underscoring that ERs and resulting payments/benefits are generated and distributed down to Hue-level stakeholders in line with the national BSP. 

How the 1.0 Mt relates to Hue
•	The 1.0 Mt is a national transfer from the multi-province ERP pool (surplus ERs from 2018-2019). It includes ERs generated within Hue's ERP area, but the transaction does not allocate “credits by province.” Actual financial flows back to provinces (including Hue) are governed by the ERP's Benefit-Sharing Plan after the buyer pays under the ERPA.

Currently, Cà Mau has not independently conducted any large-scale carbon credit trading. However, the province plays a key role in Vietnam's national carbon market strategy. Cà Mau is currently in the preparatory phase, laying the groundwork for carbon credits—particularly forest and mangrove-based (blue carbon) credits.

The provincial government has approved the 'Sustainable Forest Management and Forest Certification Project,' which includes a crucial component on developing a carbon credit market. The project aims to inventory and assess carbon stocks in forest areas and establish a transparent roadmap for selling carbon credits in both international and domestic markets.

Cà Mau's enormous potential
Cà Mau is considered Vietnam's 'gold mine' for carbon credits for the following reasons:

Largest forest area: The province has the largest area of mangrove and melaleuca forests in the country, with extremely high CO₂ sequestration capacity.
Massive carbon stocks: Experts estimate that with over 140,000 hectares of forest, Cà Mau has the potential to generate more than 10 million carbon credits annually.
High economic value: Given international market prices (typically ranging from 5 to 15 USD per credit), this resource could generate tens to hundreds of millions of USD annually for the province.
Steps currently underway
To turn this potential into reality, Cà Mau is focusing on the following key actions:

Inventory and measurement: Completing accurate measurement and calculation of carbon stocks stored in forest areas.
Legal framework development: Establishing clear mechanisms and policies for carbon credit sales, with a particular emphasis on benefit-sharing mechanisms to ensure fair compensation for forest-protecting communities and households.
Partner engagement: Actively collaborating with international organizations and businesses seeking to purchase carbon credits to offset their emissions.
In summary, Cà Mau is currently in the preparation phase and is best positioned to become one of Vietnam's and the region's leading suppliers of carbon credits.
